beliefs.practice: Read the DocumentDB/Mongo connection string only from environment (e.g., process.env.DOCUMENTDB_URI) and never commit credentials to the repository or log them; provide a .env.example with a placeholder instead.
Create and reuse a single Mongoose connection per process (share the mongoose connection across modules), close it gracefully on SIGINT/SIGTERM, and avoid creating a new connection per request.
Enable TLS/SSL for the client connection (set tls=true / ssl=true and verify the server certificate) when connecting to the managed cluster; do not disable certificate validation in production.

When running multi-document transactions, keep transactions short and limited to the minimum read/write set (fetch, check, update), avoid long-lived user input inside transactions, and commit as soon as possible to limit locks and RU costs.

Use optimistic concurrency (Mongoose versionKey / optimisticConcurrency option or manual version field) to detect concurrent updates; on version mismatch surface a clear conflict error and retry the operation by refetching the latest documents.

When performing transactions, implement a retry loop with exponential backoff and jitter that retries on transient transaction errors (e.g., MongoDB driver labels TransientTransactionError or UnknownTransactionCommitResult) and re-reads necessary documents before retrying.

Choose partition keys so that documents updated together in a transaction are colocated (same partition) where possible — for example, colocate a user's cart and that user's reservation of inventory — to avoid cross-partition transaction limits and high RU/cost.

Create indexes that match your query patterns: at minimum create a unique index on inventory.sku and an index on cart.userId (and a compound index for frequent cart queries like {userId:1, 'items.sku':1}) to avoid COLLSCANs.
Project only needed fields in reads and limit results (use .select() / projection and .limit()) to reduce RU consumption and network transfer when checking stock or rendering carts.

When decrementing inventory, check available quantity inside the same transaction (e.g., find the inventory doc, assert available >= qty, then update $inc:-qty) and throw a clear OutOfStock error if insufficient, rather than attempting blind decrements.

Use proper readConcern and writeConcern in transactions (e.g., readConcern:'snapshot' for consistent reads inside the txn and writeConcern:'majority' when durability matters) or the Mongo driver defaults designed for transactions, and be explicit about these settings in session.startTransaction.

Detect and surface specific failure modes: return a typed OutOfStock error for insufficient inventory, a Conflict/VersionMismatch error for optimistic concurrency failures, and a TransientError for retryable transaction problems so callers can react appropriately.

Monitor RU/s and query latency in the Azure portal (or cluster tools) because multi-document transactions and large reads can dramatically increase RU consumption — provision or autoscale throughput accordingly and test under load.

Prefer single-document atomic operations when possible (update with $inc, $push, $pull on the same document) rather than multi-document transactions for performance and cost; use multi-document transactions only when atomicity across documents is required.
Set appropriate Mongo client timeouts (serverSelectionTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS) and a reasonable connection pool size (maxPoolSize) to avoid hanging operations and to support expected concurrency.

For Mongoose models, enable optimisticConcurrency (or manually honor __v) so save() rejects on stale versions rather than silently overwriting; ensure transaction retry logic handles these rejections and re-fetches the authoritative state.

Avoid large transactions that touch many documents or large binary fields — split work into smaller steps, use reservation/hold patterns (reserve stock, commit later) if you need long workflows, and release holds on failure or timeout.
Use database-side unique constraints/indexes (unique index on inventory.sku) to ensure data integrity rather than relying only on application checks.

When using vector search capabilities, create an explicit vector index (choose algorithm: HNSW/IVF/DiskANN) with correct dimensionality and appropriate indexing parameters, and test recall/latency trade-offs on representative data before production use.

Use the platform's management/inspection tools (the documentdb MCP server, explain plans, index stats) to verify created indexes and query plans; iterate indexes until explain() shows index usage and no COLLSCANs for critical queries.
